forces.title: Agentic AI to significantly erode consumer credit card revenues by 2030
forces.description: Agentic AI is poised to disrupt consumer credit card revenues, potentially putting $10 billion globally at risk by 2030. This erosion could occur through payment rail substitution, automated repayment optimization, fee avoidance, and real-time foreign-exchange routing. For NBFIs engaged in consumer finance, particularly credit card issuance, this represents a significant structural challenge. The impact could be substantial, with net interchange revenue from cards in heavy markets potentially cut by 30-75% from 2025 levels by 2030.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Stablecoins and digital assets to pressure traditional card economics and margins
forces.description: The emergence and scaling of digital assets like stablecoins and tokenized deposits present an additional headwind to traditional payments and deposit revenues. These digital assets bypass established interchange fees and foreign-exchange conversion markups, directly pressuring the margins of card networks and financial institutions, including NBFIs, involved in consumer credit cards and payment services. Their growth, especially in cross-border corporate corridors, could shift float income away from commercial bank deposits and intensify competition with traditional credit card business models.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Strong card infrastructure in Western Europe to preserve consumer finance market
forces.description: Western Europe, including the UK, exhibits a "card resilient" market with highly mature credit and debit card infrastructure. This entrenched system, characterized by widespread merchant acceptance, attractive consumer rewards programs, and robust dispute resolution mechanisms, effectively preserves the card perimeter against newer payment technologies. This resilience is a tailwind for NBFIs involved in consumer credit cards, as it helps maintain their market share and business model against potential disruption from emerging A2A networks and stablecoins, with high adoption projected through 2035.
forces.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world

forces.title: Nonbank lenders and alternative financing platforms increasing corporate finance competition
forces.description: Nonbank lenders and alternative financing platforms are increasingly competing with traditional banks for corporate business, including financing mandates, foreign exchange (FX) cash, hedging flows, and complex structures like Net Asset Value (NAV) credit facilities. This signifies a structural shift in the corporate finance landscape, as clients actively reallocate wallet share based on performance and specialized capabilities. For NBFIs, this represents a significant tailwind, as they are positioned as viable alternatives to traditional banking institutions, capturing business that was previously exclusive to banks.
forces.source_title: Anchor or drift: What it takes to capture wallet share in 2026

viewpoints.title: Western Europe's mature card infrastructure to remain resilient through 2035
viewpoints.description: McKinsey views Western Europe and the UK as "card resilient" markets with mature credit and debit card infrastructure. Projections suggest high card and wallet adoption will continue through 2030 and 2035, while alternative payment rails like stablecoins and local A2A systems lag significantly. This resilience is attributed to entrenched merchant acceptance, valuable consumer rewards, and established dispute resolution mechanisms, which preserve the card perimeter. This implies NBFIs involved in consumer credit cards in these regions will continue to benefit from this stable environment, despite emerging payment technologies.
viewpoints.source_title: The 2026 Global Payments Report: Operational excellence in an invisible world
